# Evaluation Protocol

## Principle

A single “accuracy” number would hide where the system succeeds or fails. Report three layers.

## Layer A — deterministic engine correctness

**Input:** exact normalized answers generated by known procedures.

**Measure:** whether the top diagnosis equals the generating procedure and whether confidence gating behaves as specified.

**Dataset:** exhaustive or large parameterized synthetic set covering denominator combinations, simplification and collisions between rules.

**Expected:** near-perfect on identifiable patterns. Report collisions/ambiguity, not only accuracy.

## Layer B — handwriting extraction

**Input:** handwritten answer crops with ground-truth transcriptions.

**Measure:**

- exact normalized-expression accuracy;
- top-2 candidate coverage;
- step-feature precision/recall;
- unreadable detection rate.

This evaluates the Featherless vision stage, not the diagnosis.

## Layer C — controlled end-to-end pilot

**Protocol:** Recruit several volunteers. Randomly assign a procedure card, give each person a worksheet, and ask them to solve every item by that procedure in their normal handwriting. Keep one problem physically separate as held-out.

**Measure:**

- top-1 diagnosis accuracy;
- top-2 coverage;
- confidence-gated coverage and accuracy;
- held-out prediction accuracy;
- confusion matrix.

**Honest label:** “Controlled assigned-procedure pilot.” It does not prove natural classroom prevalence or educational outcomes.

## Optional Layer D — consented naturalistic examples

With teacher and student privacy consent, annotate a small set of real worksheets. Report as case studies unless sample size and annotation quality support more.

## Calibration and coverage

For thresholds 0.5–0.9, report:

- fraction of students receiving a named diagnosis;
- accuracy among diagnosed cases;
- fraction routed to more evidence.

A trustworthy system may choose lower coverage to preserve accuracy.

## Reproducibility

The repository must include:

```bash
python scripts/evaluate.py --dataset data/evaluation/controlled_pilot.csv
```

The command should produce machine-readable JSON, a CSV confusion matrix, and a PNG/SVG figure.
